description: Umbilical cable, module to instrument
notes: *** GAUGE IS OPEN AND THREE DERIVATIONS ASSUME 24 AWG. *** 0005:91 computes a ~0.34 ohm round trip, breath-sense-link.md:100 a 0.168 ohm return term, and 0003:315 a whole signal-drop table - all at 24 AWG, which this row does not specify. A stranded Cat5e PATCH lead is commonly 26 or 28 AWG, at 1.6x to 2.6x the resistance. WHAT DECIDES IT: buy the lead, read the jacket print, or measure end-to-end DC resistance at E6. Note the trap - the well-argued STRANDED requirement below is exactly what makes a thinner gauge likely, and nobody connected the two. STRANDED not solid-core: solid core work-hardens and fractures under constant flexing, which is this cable's whole life. Shielded preferred. It is a CONSUMABLE - keep spares and replace at the first intermittency

part: Ettinger 5.52.015, plain spacer M2.5 (bore 2.6, L 1.5), faced to 1.3
description: Between the key plate's underside and the key board's top face on each column: it alone sets the key board's depth

It sets the key boards' depth, switch.pcb_below_seat: drc.echo 'key-board mount sets the board depth', and 'key-board depth at the hardware's tolerance limits'. It bears on the board's top copper, so the PCB keeps copper out from under it (grown by hardware.kb_mount_float); kept off the switch cutouts by drc.echo 'key-board spacers clear of the switch cutouts'. Buy with MECH-MB-SPACER, the same part faced alike. MATERIAL: Ettinger's catalogue lists the 5.52 series as stainless steel, its article sheet for 5.52.023 as nickel-plated brass - either serves; confirm at order. DRAWINGS: datasheets/mechanical/ETTINGER-CATALOG-2024-P79-DISTANZHUELSEN-MESSING.html (the series); datasheets/mechanical/ETTINGER-005.52.015-SPACER-2.6x4.5x1.5-BRASS-NI.pdf (this part). part: PEM FHL-M2.5-10ZI self-clinching flush-head stud, low-displacement head, zinc-plated steel
description: Pressed into the bottom plate from its underside at every one of the main board's mounts, head flush; carries the spacer, the main board, and a column's standoff or an end mount's nut
notes: ONE PER MOUNT ON THE BOTTOM PLATE. COUNT: mechanical/drc.echo 'main board mounts on the bottom plate' (columns and end mounts). PRESSED INTO THE PLATE BY THE PLATE VENDOR (or on a press): hole hardware.stud_hole, NOT DEBURRED, stud inserted from the punch side, squeezed flush on a flat parallel anvil - for sheet this thin, PEM's countersunk anvil 8003302 with punch 975200997 [datasheets/mechanical/PEM-FH-SELF-CLINCHING-STUDS.pdf p.FH-18, FH-20]. Never hammered. FHL, not FH: FHL holds its data in 1.2 mm aluminium and needs 2.8 from an edge - a thumb switch's cutout, a U-bolt hole and the plate's outline all count (hardware.stud_edge; drc.echo 'bottom-plate studs clear of the plate's edges and cutouts'); rated for aluminium to HRB 80 / HB 150, so 5052 or 6061. Zinc-plated steel, not stainless: PEM's finish guide calls stainless in aluminium a significant galvanic pair and plated steel acceptable [datasheets/mechanical/PEM-TECHSHEET-CHOOSING-A-FASTENER-FINISH.pdf pp.3-4]. LENGTH 10: the plate, spacer and main board and 1.5 d into the column standoff at its shortest (hardware.stud_l; drc.echo 'column: stud thread in the standoff', 'end mounts: stud thread past the nut', 'bottom-plate studs: unthreaded shank ends inside the spacer'). TIGHTEN THE STANDOFF OR NUT ON IT TO NO MORE THAN hardware.stud_torque. IT CARRIES THE PLATES' GROUND (ADR 0025): its clinch bonds the bottom plate, and through the column's standoff and screw the key plate, to the main board's plated PWR_GND pads. DRAWING: datasheets/mechanical/PEM-FHL-M2.5-10ZI-SALES-DRAWING.pdf. US SOURCE: not yet found [UNVERIFIED - ask the plate vendor, who presses them]

part: RTV silicone - ALKOXY (alcohol) neutral cure, electronics-safe
description: Bonds the cassette into the shell - the key plate to the oak top, the bottom plate to the oak bottom - the oak top to the sides at the grooves, and the matrix diffuser
notes: NOT ACETOXY. The common hardware-store type releases acetic acid while curing, inside a closed cavity holding the boards, connectors and a pressure sensor. Compliant in shear so the oak's 0.6-0.9mm of cross-grain humidity movement does not fight the aluminium plates. BEAD IT, DO NOT BUTTER IT - cure needs atmospheric moisture and runs ~2mm/day inwards, so a trapped full-face layer never cures. Keep it off both sensor ports (ADR 0003) and out of the column screws' pockets. SERVICE IS BY CUTTING IT (ADR 0025): every joint it makes is one that may have to open, so it is the adhesive there, fresh, and nothing harder is used on them. Bond the cassette only after it has been assembled and tested on the bench
